steps.what: Process film and prints from crime or accident scenes and inspect the results

tasks.design: Retain physical film handling, processing and print inspection with the officer using photographic processing equipment in {OTHER}. Existing equipment cycles earn no new human time saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handling and image quality depend on the source material and processing conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software capability is assumed to replace physical processing.
tasks.still_hard: Damage or inappropriate processing can compromise evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise defects and preserve the original material and processing history.
tasks.altitude: No change to physical processing work is claimed.

evidence.claim: Physical film and print processing is retained; no digest source establishes a relevant automation saving.

assumptions: Boundary is processing film and prints when actually received; digital-only capture does not create a fictitious analogue baseline.

OTHER means photographic processing equipment. Officer verifies film/item identity and produces processing method, time, settings and result notes within s1's retained100 hours. Source officers supply film and custody records beforehand. Missing identity or unsuitable instructions lead to manual clarification before processing, not an inferred ready flag.
Retain native equipment functions before custom development; existing unattended cycles are runtime and not labour saved.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool or workflow is proposed.
unknowns: Whether analogue film remains in the workload
Current equipment and approved processing methods
research_questions: Is this task still performed locally, and which minutes are active handling rather than machine cycles?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0 for actual film-processing work; an absent analogue workload creates no saving.

steps.what: Take fingerprints and verify complete, correctly identified impressions

tasks.design: Keep fingerprint capture with the officer using the existing capture equipment in {OTHER}. Device feedback supports completeness checks without replacing identity or impression-quality judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correct positioning and usable impressions require physical capture and verification.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing capture equipment already supports the task.
tasks.still_hard: Damaged skin, poor impressions and uncertain identity need careful handling.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a capture should be repeated or its limitations recorded.
tasks.altitude: Capture work and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Understand the limitations of identification material

evidence.claim: Fingerprint taking retains physical positioning, identity and completeness checks; the digest's face comparison capability does not establish fingerprint capture savings.

assumptions: Boundary is taking fingerprints, not later database matching or identification decisions.

OTHER means fingerprint capture equipment. Existing case authority supplies the capture request before the task; officer verifies person/case identity and captures finger position, impression, time and quality limitations during the retained100 hours. No pre-existing usable-print flag is assumed. Unusable capture follows authorised repeat or manual procedures.
Use native equipment feedback before custom software; existing device runtime earns no new saving.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new device, tool or transferred capture duty is introduced.
unknowns: Existing electronic versus ink capture method
research_questions: Which capture failures require repeat physical work despite device feedback?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Existing electronic capture is not a new labour saving, and physical impression checks remain.

tasks.short: Advise and coordinate scene collection activities

steps.what: Serve as technical advisor and coordinate crime scene collection activities with other personnel

tasks.design: Retain technical advice and coordination with the officer using existing {TELEPHONY} and source material in {DOCS}. Advice remains tied to the actual scene and collection constraints.
tasks.previous_blocker: Collection choices depend on material, scene conditions and the investigative question.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication and source access already support the task.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting priorities or incomplete scene information require clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the limits of a collection method and negotiate a workable sequence.
tasks.altitude: Technical advice and coordination time remain unchanged.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of police and detectives

evidence.claim: Scene-specific technical advice and coordination remain human work; no digest case establishes savings for this interaction.

assumptions: Boundary is the officer's advice and coordination, not subsequent physical collection. Partner participation and legal decisions remain outside and unchanged.

Scene personnel produce observations and questions before and during the consultation; officer clarifies material, scene state, requested purpose, source versions and uncertainties within retained100 hours before giving related advice. Missing facts lead to clarification, not a generated suitability flag.
Retain native communication and source access before custom tools. No new structured capture is demanded from partners.
Zero incremental upkeep because the task and tools are unchanged.
research_questions: Are delays in collecting missing information being confused with officer labour?

already_counted.description: Context clarification, technical advice and coordination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Scene-dependent advice and coordination retain their time; no invented paperwork baseline is removed.

steps.what: Select scene features and capture verified measurements for sketches and diagrams
Draw measured geometry and labels in scene diagrams
Check scene fidelity, annotate uncertainty and approve the final diagrams

tasks.design: Configure the drawing application in {OTHER} to render only officer-verified geometry and labels. The officer retains measurements, feature selection and final scene-fidelity checks before storing the diagram in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measured coordinates could still need repeated manual plotting and labelling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native geometry import and drawing templates can render explicit coordinates without interpreting a scene.
tasks.still_hard: A precise drawing can be misleading when measurements or omitted context are wrong.
tasks.human_edge: Decide which context matters and distinguish measured, approximate and unknown positions.
tasks.altitude: Less plotting may leave more time to check scene fidelity; evidential judgement is unchanged.

reach.task: Use scene diagrams to test accounts

evidence.claim: Explicit verified coordinates can drive deterministic drawing; this is a model-knowledge design, not a digest-supported crime-scene case or measured saving.

assumptions: OTHER means a technical drawing application. Boundary covers scene specification, drawing and checking, not separate photographic capture or investigative reconstruction.

Officer produces feature IDs, coordinate frame, points/lines, dimensions, units, orientation, scale, exact labels, measurement sources and uncertainty in s1's retained40 hours. This includes all structured entry before s2. Inconsistent or missing geometry returns to manual drawing and field clarification; no free structured scene model is assumed.
Test native geometry import, labels and templates before custom code. Existing automatic plotting creates zero additional saving; no image inference or invented geometry is proposed.
Eight focal upkeep hours per100 baseline cover template checks, conversion exceptions and measurement-to-output comparisons; three other-role support hours are counted separately.
research_questions: Does structured capture plus native rendering save time after scene-fidelity checks on irregular scenes?
